decisions.reason: As a recent extension of the core offer with its own webpage, it likely meets at least minimum aspiration levels and is worth retaining while the firm learns from early customer uptake.

Because it is close to the established tariff and market-process business and was prominently presented, management would likely keep it despite some uncertainty and use organisational slack to continue testing demand.
This product fits the firm’s existing electricity-sector calculations and platform logic well, so in the absence of clear underperformance it would likely stay on the market.
Its weaker website prominence and multi-model line raise the chance of later consolidation, but its strong fit with the core platform makes continued market presence more likely than withdrawal.
The tool builds on the firm’s data, process and integration capabilities and had a dedicated page, so management would likely keep it while assessing whether it supports broader platform adoption.

This product line faces the highest pruning risk because it overlaps with other tariff-comparison offers and was only briefly mentioned, but the firm would still likely keep it for now given its close relatedness and low marginal carrying cost.
